list.help: List designs owned by the authenticated Dribbble user.
list.usage_instructions: Use `designs list` when Adam asks for shots owned by the authenticated Dribbble user. Limit with `--limit/-l`, display selected fields with `--properties/-p`, filter with `--filter/-f`, and use `--table/-t` for a readable table.

search.usage_instructions: Use `designs search QUERY` when Adam wants public Dribbble shots for a topic such as mobile app or dashboard. Pass the query as the required positional argument; control output with `--limit/-l`, `--properties/-p`, `--filter/-f`, and `--table/-t`.

get.help: Get a public Dribbble design by shot ID.
get.usage_instructions: Use `designs get DESIGN_ID` to fetch one public Dribbble shot by numeric shot ID discovered from `designs search`. Use `--properties/-p` to keep only fields such as id,title,author,html_url,image_url, or `--table/-t` for a field/value table.

download.help: Download public Dribbble design image files by shot ID.
download.usage_instructions: Use `designs download DESIGN_ID` to download all public media image files for one Dribbble shot. The numeric DESIGN_ID is required; use `--output-dir/-o` to choose the destination directory, otherwise files are written to the current directory.

designs.usage_instructions: Use `designs` for Dribbble shot records. `designs search`, `designs get`, and `designs download` read public Dribbble web pages; `designs list` uses the authenticated owner API and only returns the active user's shots.

login.help: Configure authentication credentials. Prompts for required credentials based on the tool's authentication type. For OAuth authorization code flows, opens a browser for user consent.

options.name: --profile
options.help: Profile name to save credentials to

login.usage_instructions: Use `auth login` to run the OAuth authorization-code flow for Dribbble. Use `--force/-F` to clear saved login state and re-enter the client ID/secret; `--profile/-p` selects the profile to update.

options.name: --profile
options.help: Profile name to clear credentials from

logout.usage_instructions: Use `auth logout` to clear saved Dribbble credentials for a profile. Pass `--profile/-p` when clearing a non-default profile.

status.help: Check authentication status across profiles. Performs a live round-trip for every configured credential type so the report reflects ground truth — not on-disk belief. Saved credentials whose live verification fails are reported as ``authenticated: false`` with the failure reason in ``api_test``.

options.name: --profile
options.help: Profile name to check (defaults to all profiles)

status.usage_instructions: Use `auth status` to verify saved Dribbble credentials. Read the shared profile output shape under `profiles[].credential_types.oauth_authorization_code` rather than expecting a flat authenticated field.

refresh.help: Refresh OAuth access token using stored refresh token.
refresh.usage_instructions: Use `dribbble auth refresh` for: Refresh OAuth access token using stored refresh token.

test.help: Test authentication by verifying credentials work across profiles.
test.usage_instructions: Use `auth test` for a live Dribbble credential check on the selected profile. Pass `--profile/-p` to test a specific profile.

list.help: List all profiles and show their auth types and active state.

options.name: --limit
options.help: Maximum number of profiles to return

options.name: --properties
options.help: Comma-separated list of fields to include

list.usage_instructions: Use `auth profiles list` to see all Dribbble authentication profiles. Add `--table/-t` for human-readable output.

get.help: Get details for a specific profile.

arguments.name: name
arguments.help: Profile name to get details for

get.usage_instructions: Use `auth profiles get PROFILE_NAME` to inspect one Dribbble profile. Add `--table/-t` for a field/value view.

create.help: Create a new profile from .env.example template.
create.usage_instructions: Use `auth profiles create PROFILE_NAME` to create a new Dribbble authentication profile. Use `--auth-type` only when the CLI exposes multiple credential types.

select.help: Activate a profile within its auth type.

arguments.name: name
arguments.help: Profile name to activate within its auth type

select.usage_instructions: Use `auth profiles select PROFILE_NAME` to make a Dribbble profile active. Other auth profile operations should use this nested command path.

delete.help: Delete a profile and its data.
delete.usage_instructions: Use `auth profiles delete PROFILE_NAME` to remove a Dribbble authentication profile. This is destructive for that profile's saved runtime auth state.

remove.help: Delete a profile and its data.
remove.usage_instructions: Use `dribbble auth profiles remove` for: Delete a profile and its data.

profiles.usage_instructions: Use `auth profiles` to list, inspect, create, select, and delete named Dribbble authentication profiles. Preserve the nested command path, for example `dribbble auth profiles list`.

auth.usage_instructions: Use `auth` to manage Dribbble OAuth credentials and authentication profiles. Check `auth status` before owner-only API work; public search, public get, and public download do not require owner shots to exist.

clear.help: Remove all cached responses. Deletes every file in the cache directory ({storage_dir}/cache/) and reports how many files and bytes were freed.
clear.usage_instructions: Use `cache clear` to remove cached Dribbble command responses. Use this before retesting changed public search/get/download behavior when cached output would hide a parser change.

cache.usage_instructions: Use `cache` to clear cached Dribbble read responses. Add global `--no-cache` before the command group when a fresh Dribbble request is required.

usage_instructions: Use the Dribbble CLI to authenticate with Dribbble, search public shot pages, get public shot details, download public shot images, and list the authenticated user's own shots. Commands follow `dribbble <command-group> <action>`; use `--table/-t`, `--limit/-l`, `--filter/-f`, and `--properties/-p` on list/search outputs when available.
